status_summary: Dear Colleague Letter GEN-25-03, published on the Federal Student Aid Partner Connect site on 2025-05-01, states that it supersedes GEN-22-10 and GEN-22-11 and sets a new process for changing accrediting agencies, including a finding of reasonable cause when state law requires a public institution to change accreditors and deemed approval after 30 days. The GEN-22-11 page now carries a banner saying it is maintained for historical purposes only and is not currently applicable. A proposed rule published on 2026-08-20 (91 FR 53940) would treat cause for a change as reasonable unless it is sought to evade federal requirements or avoid enforcement. No withdrawal of the 2022-07-19 letter to accrediting agencies on voluntary membership was found.

timeline.event: The Department issued Dear Colleague Letter GEN-25-03, Changes to the Approval Process for Changing Accrediting Agencies, which states that it supersedes GEN-22-10 and GEN-22-11, treats a state-law requirement to change accreditors as reasonable cause, and deems approval granted after 30 days.

The Department published a notice of proposed rulemaking, Accreditation, Innovation, and Modernization (91 FR 53940, document 2026-17001); proposed 34 CFR 600.11 would treat cause for changing accreditors as reasonable unless the change is sought to evade federal requirements, avoid enforcement, obtain eligibility unlawfully or undermine title IV integrity; comments closed 2026-09-21.

title: Rescind Dear Colleague Letters GEN 22-10 and 22-11 and the 2022 letters to accreditors
uncertainties: The GEN-25-03 page URL carries 2025-04-30 while the page prints 2025-05-01; the printed date is used. The 2022 page read is GEN-22-11 (confirmed on its own page); the GEN-22-10 page was not opened, so its banner status is inferred from the supersession statement in GEN-25-03. GEN-25-03 does not mention the 2022-07-19 letter to accrediting agencies on voluntary membership, and the 2026 proposed rule discusses voluntary membership in its section 602.13 and 602.15 proposals without naming the 2022 letter, in the portion read.
